subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Value Function: An S-Curve
description: Learn The Value Function: An S-Curve in one minute.

hook.text: Gaining $100 feels good. But losing $100 hurts about twice as much. The curve isn't symmetrical.

buildup.text: Prospect theory's value function is S-shaped: concave for gains, convex and steeper for losses.

discovery.text: The steeper loss side means losses loom larger than equivalent gains. This asymmetry drives most decisions.

twist.text: The curve also flattens at extremes. Gaining $1 million vs $1.1 million feels tiny. The first million matters most.

climax.text: This simple S-curve explains gambling, insurance buying, risk aversion for gains, and risk seeking for losses.

punchline.text: One curve explains a thousand irrational choices.

quiz.question: What shape is the prospect theory value function?
options: S-shaped, steeper on the loss side
